phases.message: I'm Marisol Teague. This is my mail. Read every message from the last few weeks. The charges I don't recognise are Brightwave Telecom, Hexa Outfitters, Corvane Utility Pay, Northpoint Warranty, Eldervale Services and Brindle Electronics, and the 400 dollars at the cash machine on 28 September. Don't do anything yet: I'll send you to my bank, my payment app and my credit card next.
This is my bank. Read its rules for unauthorised transfers and errors, my statements, my transactions on every page, and my claims. Don't report anything yet.
This is my payment app. Read its activity.
This is my credit card. Read its charges.

Back at my bank. Report each transfer from my account that I did not authorise, with what I am liable for under the rules, and where the bank has let a claim of mine run past its time, ask it for the provisional credit. Leave out what I did myself or allowed, what has been refunded or is about to be, what is not a transfer from this account, and anything the bank is not yet late on. Then tell me what you reported and what you left alone and why.

rules.text: Ledgerwren bank, the rules for unauthorised transfers and errors on Marisol's checking account. Friday 9 October 2026. Topics: authorised, liability, errors, cards, statements.

Friday 9 October 2026. A transfer is unauthorised when someone other than the customer starts it without actual authority and she gets no benefit (12 CFR 1005.2(m)). A transfer she starts herself is authorised, even when a scammer persuaded her to start it. A transfer by a person she gave her card or login to is authorised until she tells the bank that the person may no longer use it. A transfer started by someone who got her card, code or login from her by fraud or robbery is unauthorised (Supplement I, comment 2(m)-3). A transfer the merchant has refunded, or has promised to refund, is not an error in the bank's records.

Friday 9 October 2026. If a card, PIN, code or login is lost, stolen or taken by fraud, and she tells the bank within two business days after the day she learns of it, she is liable for the lesser of 50 dollars or the unauthorised transfers made before she told us. After that she can be liable for up to 500 dollars. When no access device was lost or stolen (a card number copied while she still has the card, or an ACH debit she never agreed to), those two limits do not apply: she is not liable for the transfer if she reports it within 60 days after the statement that shows it was sent. Business days leave out weekends and federal holidays; Monday 12 October 2026 is a holiday.

Friday 9 October 2026. She must tell the bank of an error within 60 days after the statement that first shows it was sent (12 CFR 1005.11(b)); a report in this portal is written notice, and an oral notice is confirmed in writing within 10 business days. The bank then has 10 business days to investigate and tell her the result, or up to 45 days if it credits the amount to her account within the 10 business days (1005.11(c)). If it finds no error it explains in writing and she may ask for the documents it used (1005.11(d)). A claim the bank has neither answered nor credited by the end of its 10 business days is late, and she can ask for the provisional credit.

Friday 9 October 2026. These rules cover transfers from Marisol's checking account: debit card, ATM, ACH and payment-app top-ups. A credit card is a different account at a different company. A charge on it is a billing dispute under Regulation Z (12 CFR 1026.12(b)) and is made to the card company, not as an error here.

Friday 9 October 2026. A statement is sent on the second of the month after the month it covers. The 60 days for a transfer run from the day the statement showing it was sent. See the statements list for the dates.
